engine.title: Stop buying strength that has already run
engine.body: The 4H RSI ceiling for longs was 75. Splitting every closed trade by the RSI recorded at entry showed the engine bleeding above 65 and profitable below it. The ceiling is now 65.
engine.note: Holds in both halves of the sample and at every cut point tested (60, 65, 70), so it is not one lucky threshold. The threshold was still chosen from this sample, so treat the size as an upper bound.

engine.title: A break-even stop would not have helped
engine.body: The median losing trade was +1.44R in profit before it reversed, and 59% touched a full +1R first. That looks like an obvious fix: move the stop to entry once price pays 1R. Re-walking every trade bar by bar, with winners subject to the same rule, says otherwise.
engine.note: The first version of this test only altered losers, which guarantees a positive answer. Correcting it reversed the conclusion. Nothing tested cleared one standard error, so no stop rule was adopted.

engine.title: Trades were being closed at prices that never traded
engine.body: The grader had never resolved a single trade — an exception was being swallowed silently — leaving a fallback path that could book an exit at a bar from before the signal existed. Every closed trade was re-graded against bars that actually printed.
evidence: exits corrected to a real price
engine.note: This moved the headline number against me. It is published anyway, because the earlier number was not real. Pre-correction data is kept in the repo rather than deleted.

engine.title: A first target must pay back the risk
engine.body: T1 was whichever structural level sat nearest the entry, with no distance test. One signal shipped a T1 worth 0.19R against its own stop, printed beside an R:R of 2.41 quoted off T2. T1 must now return at least 1R.

chess.title: Opening Principle #2: Develop Your Pieces
chess.body: In the first 10 moves, move each piece once. Get knights out before bishops (Ng1-f3, Nb1-c3). Don't move the same piece twice. Don't bring the queen out early — she gets chased. Goal: by move 8, have 3-4 pieces off the back rank. Development = time. Time = initiative.

wisdom.title: On Failure
wisdom.body: You will fail your daughter sometimes. You'll be impatient. You'll miss something important. You'll get it wrong. What matters is the repair: the apology, the return, the consistent showing up after the mistake. Children don't need perfect parents. They need parents who can say sorry and mean it.

book.author: John Doerr
book.lesson: Doerr profiles how OKRs drove Google's 10× growth. The key principle: set 'stretch goals' that are uncomfortable — goals that you're not sure you can achieve. A goal you can definitely hit in normal circumstances is not ambitious enough. Google's rule: OKRs should score 0.6-0.7 (60-70% achieved) consistently. If you're hitting 1.0 every quarter, your targets are too conservative. This is counterintuitive for finance professionals trained to hit budgets. In innovation contexts, the right level of ambition makes success feel slightly out of reach — that tension drives breakthrough thinking, not incremental improvement.
book.key_quote: If you never miss a target, your targets are too safe. Set goals that force you to change how you work, not just do more of what you already do.
book.action: Set one 10× goal for your career in the next 2 years. Not 10% better — 10× different. What would have to change for that to happen?
crux: OKRs = Objective (where to go) + Key Results (how you know you got there).
Objectives are qualitative and inspiring. Key results are numeric and time-bound.
If it has no number, it is not a key result.
Focus: 3–5 objectives per cycle. More than that means no priorities.
Align transparently. Everyone's OKRs visible, including the CEO's.
Roughly half of OKRs should be bottom-up, or you get compliance instead of commitment.
Commit publicly. Visibility is what converts a goal into an obligation.
Stretch: aspirational OKRs should land around 70%. Consistent 100% means you set them too low.
Separate committed OKRs (must hit 100%) from aspirational ones (70% is success).
Never tie OKRs to compensation. It corrupts the target-setting immediately.
Track continuously — grade, then continue, update, start over, or stop.
CFRs — Conversations, Feedback, Recognition — replace annual reviews.
OKRs are a vessel, not the content. Bad strategy with good OKRs still fails.
learnings: A goal without a number is a wish with better vocabulary.
Transparency is what makes alignment happen without meetings.
70% on a hard target beats 100% on an easy one.
Linking goals to bonuses guarantees sandbagged goals.
examples: Intel's Operation Crush retook the microprocessor market from Motorola in 1980, coordinated entirely through OKRs across every function.
Google adopted OKRs at ~40 people and has published them quarterly since. Chrome's 20M→111M user objective drove the browser's whole roadmap.
The Gates Foundation uses OKRs on a $20bn scale to make measurable what was previously a stated intention.
adapt: Q3 objective: land the Dubai offer. KRs: 40 targeted applications, 12 first-round calls, 3 finals. Numbers, not effort.
Codex KR: 20 paying customers at $47, not 'launch the product'.
Trading KR: expectancy above +0.15R over 100 live signals. Grade it, then stop or continue.
Grade quarterly and write the number down even when it's 40%. Especially then.

minimalism.title: Subscription Audit
minimalism.body: Recurring charges are the most invisible clutter you own — designed to be forgotten. The average person carries several they cannot name.
minimalism.action: Open your statement. Cancel every subscription you cannot justify out loud.
minimalism.label: Minimalism

etiquette.title: Leave Well
etiquette.body: How you exit a job, a room, or a conversation is what people remember. Notice periods honoured, handovers documented, no bridges burned. The world is smaller than it feels.
etiquette.action: Leave your next meeting with a clear closing sentence, not a trailing off.
etiquette.label: Etiquette

stillness.title: Serve Without Being Seen
stillness.body: Do one useful thing today that nobody will attribute to you. Every tradition prescribes this because it is the fastest available correction to the ego.
stillness.action: One anonymous useful act. Tell no one.
stillness.label: Stillness

model.title: Regression To The Mean
model.body: Extreme results are followed by less extreme ones, with no cause required. Most 'the intervention worked' stories are regression wearing a costume.
model.action: Before crediting a change, ask what would have happened anyway.
model.label: Mental Model

drill.title: Rule of 72
drill.body: Years to double = 72 ÷ rate. At 12%, six years. At 8%, nine. Lets you sanity-check any growth or return claim instantly, without a spreadsheet.
drill.action: Apply it to five return rates. Then invert: what rate doubles in 4 years?
drill.label: Drill

health.title: Visceral Fat Is The One That Matters
health.body: Fat around the organs is metabolically active and drives insulin resistance. Waist-to-height under 0.5 is the simplest useful screen — better than BMI, which cannot distinguish muscle from fat.
health.action: Measure waist and height. Divide. Should be under 0.5.
health.label: Health

quote.name: Thomas Edison
quote.quote: I have not failed. I've just found 10,000 ways that won't work.

lesson.lesson: Discipline is the bridge between goals and accomplishment.

case.title: McDonald's: Real Estate, Not Burgers
case.story: Ray Kroc's insight: McDonald's isn't a food company — it's a real estate company. Franchise owners pay rent on land McDonald's owns.
case.lesson: The most valuable part of a business is often hidden. Always ask: what are we actually selling? Who really controls the profit pool in our industry?

fpna.title: Headcount Planning
fpna.body: FTE cost = Salary × 1.3–1.5. Always model hiring lag — 60–90 days from approval to productive.

cfo.title: Power BI for Finance Leaders
cfo.body: Build a CFO dashboard: P&L vs Budget, Cashflow waterfall, Working Capital trend, Revenue bridge. Link to ERP via DirectQuery. Refresh daily. Present this in interviews as your personal project. It shows initiative + technical skill + commercial sense.

money_hack.title: Tax-Loss Harvesting
money_hack.body: Book losses at year-end to offset LTCG. Reinvest post 30 days. Saves 10–15% tax.

dubai.title: The reference call decides it
dubai.body: Gulf groups check references properly, and they call the person you name. A manager who says 'he was good' loses you the band. A manager who says 'he cut our forecast error from 12% to 4%' wins you the counter.
dubai.targets: Brief your references. Give them the number you want said.
dubai.action: Pick two. Send each a three-line note on what the role needs.

desk.productivity: Under-promise, over-deliver. Every time. Build a reputation.

father.title: Learn her tired signals
father.do: Watch for the specific cues before crying — ear pulling, gaze aversion, a particular whine.
father.why: Catching the window before the overtired threshold is the difference between a 5-minute settle and a 40-minute one. Every baby's signal set is different; only observation finds hers.

father.title: One-word labels
father.do: Use single words for objects she sees constantly — 'cup', 'light', 'dog' — rather than full sentences.
father.why: Isolated words are easier to segment from the speech stream. Mix with full sentences; she needs both the target and the grammar around it.

life_wisdom.teaching: The second great vow. Jain teaching qualifies it sharply: truth that causes harm is not virtue, so silence is sometimes the higher form of satya.
life_wisdom.apply: Before delivering a hard truth, ask whether you are serving accuracy or serving yourself. Both can be honest; only one is useful.

life_wisdom.teaching: Sati literally means 'to remember' — remembering to notice what is actually happening, rather than the narrative running over it.
life_wisdom.apply: Once today, mid-task, stop and name what you are actually doing versus what you told yourself you would be doing. The gap is the data.

speaking.title: Own the accent
speaking.drill: Read a page aloud focusing only on the final consonant of each word, at normal speed.
speaking.why: Clarity comes from finishing words, not from changing your accent. Endings are where intelligibility is lost.

interview_tech.q: Explain contribution margin versus gross margin and when each misleads.
interview_tech.a: Gross margin is revenue less cost of goods — it answers whether you bought and priced well. Contribution margin deducts all variable costs, including logistics, payment fees, markdown and returns — it answers whether the sale was worth making. Gross margin misleads for high-return or bulky goods; contribution misleads when 'variable' costs are actually committed in the short run, which makes closure decisions look better on paper than in cash. Use gross margin for buying decisions and contribution for range and channel decisions.

interview_tech.q: What is the cash conversion cycle for a fashion retailer, and how would you cut it 15 days?
interview_tech.a: CCC = DIO + DSO − DPO. Fashion retail is inventory-heavy and near-zero DSO, so it is mostly DIO minus DPO. To cut 15 days: shorten the buying calendar and increase in-season replenishment so you commit later; push slow lines to markdown earlier rather than holding for full price; renegotiate supplier terms from 60 to 90 days in exchange for volume commitment; and consolidate SKUs — every incremental SKU carries safety stock. Quantify it: on AED 400M COGS, 15 days is roughly AED 16M of cash released.

interview_soft.q: How do you handle a request from the CEO that you believe is unethical?
interview_soft.a: Slow it down without escalating to confrontation. First assume miscommunication and restate what you understood — a surprising share of these resolve there. If it holds, state your objection privately, in writing, with the specific standard or law engaged. Offer the compliant alternative that gets closest to the commercial aim. If pressed, escalate to the audit committee chair. Say plainly that you would resign rather than sign something you believe is false — the willingness is the answer they are testing for.

interview_soft.q: A peer takes credit for your team's work in front of the CEO. What do you do?
interview_soft.a: Not in the room. Afterwards, directly and without an audience: describe what you observed, not their motive, and say what you need going forward. If it repeats, correct it factually in the moment — 'just to add, the modelling on that was Priya's team' — which is a contribution rather than an accusation. Escalating first, or absorbing it silently and resenting it, are both worse. They are testing composure and whether you protect your team.
